My 15-Day Ear Treatment Journey

I want to share my experience because it might help someone facing the same problem.

It started when I had severe pain in my ear and didn’t know what to do. I decided to put a few drops of oil in my ear. After two days, the pain went away, and I felt fine. But soon after, a new problem started my ear became completely clogged with wax, and I couldn’t hear anything. I thought it would clear up on its own, but even after 10 days, there was no improvement.

I got really worried and started searching online for solutions. I tried several exercises and remedies I found on Google, but nothing helped. It was a very difficult time because I could only hear from one ear. Finally, I decided to visit an ENT specialist.

*World Obesity Day: Obesity & Obstructive Sleep Apnea – A Silent Connection*

Obesity is more than a number on the weighing scale — it significantly impacts breathing during sleep. One of the most serious yet under-diagnosed consequences is Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA).

Excess body weight, especially around the neck and upper airway, narrows the breathing passage. During sleep, these tissues collapse more easily, causing repeated pauses in breathing. This leads to loud snoring, choking episodes at night, poor-quality sleep, and excessive daytime fatigue.

Studies show that obesity is the strongest risk factor for OSA. A higher Body Mass Index (BMI) and increased neck circumference markedly increase the risk. Untreated OSA can contribute to hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, reduced concentration, mood changes, and even increased surgical risks.

The encouraging news? Even a 5–10% reduction in body weight can significantly improve sleep apnea severity. Weight loss, lifestyle modification, CPAP therapy, and in select cases, surgical intervention can dramatically improve quality of life.
If you experience loud snoring, daytime sleepiness, morning headaches, or unrefreshing sleep — don’t ignore it.

On this World Obesity Day, take a step toward healthier weight and better sleep.
🩺 Breathe better. Sleep deeper. Live healthier.

The middle ear plays a crucial role in hearing by transmitting sound from the outer ear to the inner ear. It includes structures like the eardrum and ossicles (small bones), which are essential for proper auditory function. Conditions affecting the middle ear can lead to hearing loss, discomfort, and other complications.

The glottis is a crucial part of the voice box (larynx) that plays a central role in producing sound and protecting the airway during swallowing. It consists of the vocal cords and the space between them, allowing air to pass while enabling speech and breathing functions.

Problems affecting the glottis, such as inflammation, nodules, or vocal cord dysfunction, can lead to hoarseness, difficulty speaking, throat discomfort, or breathing issues. Early assessment by an ENT specialist is important to identify underlying causes and prevent complications.
